svg.title: Share of each library's downloads at a new release or later, day by day for thirty days after release, 37 of the most downloaded Python libraries, releases of April to August 2026
svg.desc: A line chart with one line for each of 37 Python libraries. The horizontal axis is days since a release, from 0 to 30; the vertical axis is the share of that day's downloads of the library that were the new release or a later one, the median over the library's releases, from 0 to 100 per cent, with a dashed line at half. Every line starts lower on the day of release than the day after, rises on that next day, and then runs nearly flat for the rest of the month. 26 lines, in blue, are libraries where most releases reached half within two days; they sit between about 49 and 85 per cent from day 1 onwards. 11 lines, in orange, are libraries where none did; they sit between about 2 and 37 per cent all month: aiobotocore 2, boto3 7, litellm 9, grpcio-status 10, fsspec 21, botocore 23, protobuf 25, pandas 28, pytest 29, numpy 30, s3transfer 34 per cent on day 1. ClickPy's copy of the Python Package Index download log, read 28 September 2026.
